summary: Hamburg Helmut Schmidt Airport (HAM/EDDH) is located in Fuhlsbüttel, about 8.5 km north of central Hamburg. Opened in 1911, it is one of Germany's oldest civil airports and was renamed in 2016 after Hamburg-born former Chancellor Helmut Schmidt. It serves as a base for Eurowings and offers direct S-Bahn service to the city.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Hamburg Airport to the city center?
A: Take the S-Bahn S1 from Hamburg Airport station to Hamburg Hauptbahnhof; the journey takes about 25 minutes and trains run frequently.

Q: Which terminals does Hamburg Airport have?
A: HAM has Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, linked by the central Airport Plaza. Both handle domestic and international flights; check screens for your check-in and gate.

Q: Is there luggage storage at Hamburg Airport?
A: Yes, left-luggage and luggage storage services are available in the terminal area; hours and prices can vary, so check with the airport information desk.

Q: What airlines fly from Hamburg Airport?
A: Airlines include Eurowings, Lufthansa, Ryanair, easyJet, Condor, and others, with a mix of European and selected leisure routes. Check the airport website for current destinations.
transport_tips: The S-Bahn S1 is the fastest and most reliable link to central Hamburg, running every 10 minutes to Hauptbahnhof in about 25 minutes. Taxis and ride-hailing are available outside the terminals and take 25–40 minutes depending on traffic. Several local bus lines also serve the airport, including night buses, but the S-Bahn is usually the best option.
local_tip: A frequent-visitor tip: use the S-Bahn S1 from the city rather than driving, and buy your HVV ticket in the HVV app before boarding—there are no gates, but fare inspectors do check.
